next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar

glance_notes.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The voter registration deadline for Missouri's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 7, 2026.

glance_notes.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — How to Vote
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse In-Person Absentee Voting: Missouri allows registered voters to cast a no-excuse absentee ballot in person during the two weeks before an election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, that period begins October 20 and continues through November 2 at locations designated by the local election authority.

Photo ID Required: Missouri requires an accepted government-issued photo ID for a regular in-person ballot. A voter without acceptable photo identification on Election Day may cast a provisional ballot. That ballot can count if the voter returns with acceptable identification or if the election authority verifies the voter's identity through the signature-verification procedure required by state law.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Missouri residents may register through their local election authority, at designated government agencies, by mail or through Missouri's online voter registration system when the applicant can provide the electronic signature required by the state system. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, a Missouri resident and at least 17 years and 6 months old. A person must be 18 years old by Election Day to vote. A person who is confined under a sentence of imprisonment, on probation or on parole after conviction of a felony is not eligible to vote until the applicable disqualification ends. A person convicted of a felony or misdemeanor connected with the right of suffrage is disqualified from voting unless pardoned.
register.glance_value: Register online, by mail or through local officials
register.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: Missouri registration eligibility includes citizenship, Missouri residence and the state's age requirements. Missouri's felony rules are more restrictive than states that restore voting rights immediately upon release from incarceration: a person remains disqualified while on probation or parole after a felony conviction. A separate disqualification applies to convictions connected with the exercise of suffrage unless pardoned.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the Missouri Secretary of State's voter registration lookup to check whether you are registered and review your voter information. If your information is missing or incorrect, contact your local election authority. Missouri's local election authorities maintain voter registration records.
check_registration.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — Voter Registration Lookup
check_registration.internal_note: Missouri's elections are decentralized among 116 local election jurisdictions. The Secretary of State's Go Vote Missouri portal directs voters to the official registration lookup and local election authorities for registration-record questions.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: The voter registration deadline for Missouri's November 3, 2026 General Election is Wednesday, October 7, 2026. Missouri does not provide general Election Day voter registration, so eligible residents who want to participate in the General Election should complete registration by the October 7 deadline.
deadlines.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — 2026 Election Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: The Secretary of State's official 2026 Election Calendar directly lists October 7, 2026 as the last day to register for the November 3 General Election. The calendar cites RSMo 115.135.1 as the statutory basis.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use the Missouri Secretary of State's Voter Information Lookup to find your assigned polling place when information is available for your jurisdiction. Election Day voters generally must vote at their assigned polling place. If the state lookup does not provide your location or you need confirmation, contact your local election authority before Election Day.
polling_place.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — Voter Information Lookup
polling_place.internal_note: The Secretary of State's Election Day FAQ states that a voter may be able to find the assigned polling place through the Voter Information Lookup and can vote only at the assigned polling place, subject to the state's central-polling-place procedures when there is a problem. Because local election authorities administer polling locations, voters should verify the location before Election Day.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Missouri's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. Voters who are in line at 7:00 p.m. are allowed to vote. Missouri requires accepted photo identification to cast a regular in-person ballot. A voter who does not have acceptable photo identification may cast a provisional ballot under state law. The provisional ballot can count if the voter satisfies Missouri's identification or signature-verification requirements.
election_day.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — Election Day FAQs
election_day.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly establishes 6:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. polling hours and confirms that voters in line at 7:00 p.m. may vote. IMPORTANT 2026 change: RSMo 115.427 was amended effective August 28, 2026. The current statute requires one of the listed forms of photo identification for a regular ballot and provides a provisional-ballot procedure when the voter lacks that ID. Older Missouri guidance describing a regular-ballot option using secondary identification may be outdated after the August 28, 2026 statutory amendment.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Missouri polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. Anyone who is in line at the polling place by 7:00 p.m. is allowed to vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — Election Day FAQs
polling_hours.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current Election Day FAQ directly states that polls open at 6:00 a.m., close at 7:00 p.m., and voters in line at 7:00 p.m. are permitted to vote.

early_voting.label: No-Excuse In-Person Absentee Voting
early_voting.content: Missouri does not use a separate statutory system generally labeled early voting, but registered voters may cast a no-excuse absentee ballot in person during the two weeks before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, no-excuse in-person absentee voting begins October 20 and continues through November 2 at locations designated by the voter's local election authority. An accepted photo ID is required when voting absentee in person.
early_voting.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — How to Vote
early_voting.internal_note: Missouri law describes this process as no-excuse absentee voting rather than a separate early-voting system. The Secretary of State states that no-excuse in-person absentee voting is available from the second Tuesday before an election through the day before Election Day. For November 3, 2026, those dates are October 20-November 2. Current RSMo 115.427 applies the photo-ID requirement to in-person absentee voting. Local election authorities establish locations and operating hours.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Missouri requires a qualifying reason when requesting an absentee ballot that will be returned by mail. Qualifying circumstances include absence from the election jurisdiction on Election Day, incapacity or confinement because of illness or physical disability, religious belief or practice, employment as an election authority or by an election authority at a location other than the voter's own polling place, incarceration when all voting qualifications are retained, participation in an address confidentiality program, and being age 65 or older. A mail or fax request for an absentee ballot must reach the local election authority by 5:00 p.m. on the second Wednesday before the election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, that deadline is October 21. Completed absentee ballots must be received by the local election authority by the close of polls on Election Day.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Reason required by mail; request by October 21
absentee_mail.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — How to Vote
absentee_mail.internal_note: Missouri's no-excuse option applies only to in-person absentee voting during the final two weeks before Election Day. Absentee voting by mail continues to require a statutory reason. The Secretary of State directly establishes the 5:00 p.m. second-Wednesday request deadline. Some absentee ballots require notarization, while exemptions apply to categories including military/overseas voters and certain permanently disabled voters and caregivers. UOCAVA voters have separate procedures.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Missouri requires voters casting a regular ballot in person to present an accepted photo ID. Accepted identification includes a nonexpired Missouri driver's license; a nonexpired or nonexpiring Missouri nondriver license; a qualifying photo identification document issued by the United States or Missouri that is unexpired or expired after the most recent General Election; or qualifying photo identification issued by the Missouri National Guard, U.S. Armed Forces, including the Space Force, or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. A voter without one of these forms of identification may cast a provisional ballot. The provisional ballot can count if the voter returns with acceptable identification or if the election authority verifies the voter's identity by comparing the ballot-envelope signature with the signature on file and determines that the voter was eligible.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID required; provisional ballot available
voter_id.internal_note: This section is based on the version of RSMo 115.427 effective August 28, 2026, which is especially important because older Secretary of State pages and older copies of the statute may describe previous identification procedures. The new version specifically includes Space Force identification and changes the no-ID procedure to a provisional ballot rather than the older secondary-ID regular-ballot procedure. Reverify before publication because this statutory change took effect only two days before this record was prepared.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Every Missouri polling place must provide an accessible voting system for voters with disabilities, including audiovisual accessibility such as an audio ballot and enlarged on-screen text. A voter with limited mobility may request curbside voting outside the polling place. A voter who cannot read or write, is blind or has another physical disability that prevents independent voting may choose someone to provide assistance or request assistance from a bipartisan team of poll workers. Voters with a permanent physical disability may also ask their local election authority to place them on a list that automatically sends an absentee ballot application before each election.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible systems, curbside voting and assistance
accessible_voting.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — Election Day FAQs
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly confirms accessible voting systems at every polling place, curbside voting for voters with limited mobility, personal assistance and bipartisan poll-worker assistance. The state's How to Vote page also confirms the permanent absentee application list for voters with permanent physical disabilities.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Missouri provides a Military and Overseas Voting Access Portal for eligible members of the Uniformed Services, National Guard and federal service, qualifying spouses and dependents, and Missouri voters living overseas. Covered voters may use the portal or a Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is available in qualifying circumstances. Absentee ballots are available 46 days before an election. Most military and overseas voters must return voted ballots by mail, but eligible voters serving or living overseas in a combat zone, hostile-fire area or imminent-danger area may return a ballot by mail, fax, email or through the state portal. Military and overseas absentee ballots must reach the local election authority no later than noon Central Time on the Friday after the election.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, FWAB and military/overseas portal available
military_overseas.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Voting Access Portal
military_overseas.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current portal directly identifies eligible categories, registration and ballot-request methods, the 46-day ballot-availability period, electronic transmission options for qualifying hostile-zone voters and the noon-Central Friday-after-election receipt deadline. It also states that active military members and dependents who miss the ordinary registration deadline may still vote for federal offices only under applicable state and federal law.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Missouri at a qualifying residence where they meet the state's residency requirements. A student living away from that registered address who will be outside the election jurisdiction on Election Day may qualify to vote absentee. Missouri voters should maintain only one voting residence and should update their registration after establishing a new permanent voting address.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may register at one qualifying Missouri residence
student_voting.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — Register to Vote
student_voting.internal_note: Missouri registration is residence-based. The Secretary of State's absentee rules allow voting absentee when the voter will be absent from the jurisdiction on Election Day, which can apply to students living away from their registered Missouri residence. The reader-facing text deliberately avoids claiming that merely attending a Missouri college automatically establishes Missouri voting residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Missouri voters may be able to view their sample ballot through the Secretary of State's Voter Information Lookup. Sample ballots are also available at polling places and local election authority offices. Missouri requires sample ballots to be published before elections, and some local election authorities also mail sample ballots to registered voters. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's election jurisdiction and districts, voters should verify the ballot that applies to their registered address.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Check the Voter Information Lookup or local election authority
sample_ballot.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — Election Day FAQs
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Secretary of State's Election Day FAQ directly states that sample ballots may be available through the Voter Information Lookup, at polling places and at local election authority offices. It also states that sample ballots must be printed twice before each election in newspapers of general circulation and that some jurisdictions mail them to registered voters. Reverify once November ballot information is finalized.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Missouri Secretary of State, Elections Division, James C. Kirkpatrick State Information Center, 600 W. Main Street, Jefferson City, MO 65101. Elections Division phone: 800-669-8683 or 573-751-2301. For voter-specific questions involving registration, polling places or absentee voting, contact your local election authority.
contact.internal_note: Missouri commonly presents the toll-free elections number as 800-NOW-VOTE, corresponding to 800-669-8683. Missouri elections are administered through 116 local election jurisdictions, so voter-specific registration, polling-place and absentee-ballot questions are often handled by the appropriate local election authority. No unverified email address is inserted into reader-facing content.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Missouri Secretary of State's Go Vote Missouri website for official statewide voting information, including voter registration, registration lookup, polling locations, absentee voting, Election Day rules, military and overseas voting and election dates. Missouri elections are administered through 116 local election jurisdictions, and local election authorities maintain voter registration records and administer local, state and federal elections within their jurisdictions.
official_resources.glance_value: Secretary of State & local election authorities
official_resources.source_name: Missouri Secretary of State — Go Vote Missouri
official_resources.internal_note: Official 2026 Election Calendar: [https://www.sos.mo.gov/elections/calendar.html](https://www.sos.mo.gov/elections/calendar.html). Official How to Vote guidance: [https://www.sos.mo.gov/elections/goVoteMissouri/howtovote](https://www.sos.mo.gov/elections/goVoteMissouri/howtovote). Official Election Day FAQ: [https://www.sos.mo.gov/elections/govotemissouri/electionday](https://www.sos.mo.gov/elections/govotemissouri/electionday). Official Military and Overseas Voting Access Portal: [https://s1.sos.mo.gov/elections/goVoteMissouri/registeroverseas](https://s1.sos.mo.gov/elections/goVoteMissouri/registeroverseas). Current Missouri voter-ID statute effective August 28, 2026: [https://www.revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=115.427](https://www.revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=115.427). The voter-ID statute received special scrutiny because a new version took effect August 28, 2026. All source_url values are bare URL strings, and all reader-facing content uses plain text with no Markdown hyperlink syntax.
